dedupe_keys.name: illinois waterway lock closures reduced vessel traffic water quality and fish habitat use

description: This study by Michael Spear and co-authors at the Illinois Natural History Survey and the USGS Upper Midwest Environmental Sciences Center (Science of the Total Environment, 2024) uses the temporary maintenance closure of lock and dam systems on the Illinois Waterway, which halted commercial vessel traffic along the river, to measure the ecological effect of large vessel traffic. Coverage: the Illinois River before, during and after a months-long, near-complete pause in large vessel traffic, with over 3,600 water quality samples and 1,300 fish community samples from main and side channels. The traffic reduction coincided with a 33% fall in turbidity and with sound-sensitive and rheophilic fishes, and gizzard shad, the most abundant species, making more use of strata near the navigation corridor. The authors conclude that intense vessel traffic can have large physical and biological effects on big rivers, and that the growth of inland shipping needs monitoring and mitigation. Format and access: an open access article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: one river and one closure period; other conditions also changed during the closure. The measured response can be used to add environmental costs of barge traffic to waterway traffic and maintenance scheduling models. It relates to the lower Mississippi waterway digital twin and the Inland Electronic Navigational Charts in the catalogue.
